podcast.body: Released in 1971, this was Billy Joel's debut album. Due to his "young and naive" state, he "signed away the rights to his own songs." Compounding this, the album was "recorded at too high of a speed," resulting in it sounding "a little bit like Alvin in the chipmunks." This experience left him "mortified and furious," prompting him to leave his record label and move from New York to Los Angeles. "His first album was Cold Springs Harbor which was released in 1971. Being young and naive he signed away the rights to his own songs and to make matters worse. The album was recorded at too high of a speed."

srcs.episode: Ep. 51 - The Softer Side of 70s Rock
